cards.statement: Microsoft Purview Data Map can catalog data sources across Azure, other clouds, and on-premises systems.
cards.explanation: Microsoft Purview Data Map supports data discovery across hybrid and multicloud environments, so teams can find sources in more than one environment.

cards.statement: A Microsoft Purview Data Map scan copies the source's data into the catalog for direct querying.
cards.explanation: A Microsoft Purview Data Map scan ingests metadata such as schemas and classifications into the catalog; it does not create a queryable copy of source data.
cards.misconception: A Data Map scan imports source datasets for querying.

source.title: Scans and ingestion in Data Map

cards.statement: Azure Policy evaluates resources against assigned rules and reports their compliance state.
cards.explanation: Azure Policy assesses resources against policy assignments and makes noncompliant resources visible for governance.

cards.statement: An Azure Policy deny effect blocks a create or update request that violates the assigned rule.
cards.explanation: The deny effect prevents a noncompliant Azure Resource Manager request from completing when a resource is created or updated.

cards.statement: An Azure Policy assignment on a resource group evaluates resources in its sibling groups.
cards.explanation: An Azure Policy assignment at a resource group applies within that group's scope, not to other resource groups beside it.
cards.misconception: A policy assignment on one resource group governs other resource groups at the same level.

cards.statement: Azure Policy remediation tasks can bring existing resources into compliance with a modify policy.
cards.explanation: A remediation task applies a modify policy's changes to existing noncompliant resources; evaluation alone does not update them.

source.title: Details of the policy remediation task structure

cards.statement: An Azure Policy assignment grants users permission to create resources in its scope.
cards.explanation: Azure Policy governs resource compliance. Azure RBAC grants users or identities permission to create resources within a scope.
cards.misconception: A policy assignment grants access like a role assignment.

cards.statement: A Delete lock permits a subscription Owner to delete the protected resource directly.
cards.explanation: A Delete lock blocks direct deletion even for a subscription Owner. A user with the required permission can remove the lock first.
cards.misconception: Subscription Owner bypasses a Delete lock.

source.title: Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure

cards.statement: A Read-only lock blocks control-plane updates to an Azure resource.
cards.explanation: A Read-only lock prevents control-plane changes, such as updates to the protected resource, even for users with broad Azure RBAC permissions.

source.title: Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure

cards.statement: A resource lock blocks direct data-plane writes to blobs in a protected storage account.
cards.explanation: Azure resource locks restrict control-plane operations. A lock on a storage account does not block direct data-plane writes to its blobs.
cards.misconception: A storage account lock also blocks blob data writes.

source.title: Lock your Azure resources to protect your infrastructure

cards.statement: Azure portal dashboards use one shared layout across users of a subscription.
cards.explanation: Azure portal dashboards are customizable; users have private dashboards by default and can choose to share one.
cards.misconception: A subscription has one common portal dashboard for its users.

source.title: Create a dashboard in the Azure portal

cards.statement: Azure Cloud Shell requires a locally installed terminal application to manage Azure resources.
cards.explanation: Azure Cloud Shell provides an authenticated, browser-accessible shell for managing Azure resources.
cards.misconception: Cloud Shell requires a local terminal installation.

cards.statement: Azure CLI can run Azure management commands from a shell script on Linux or macOS.
cards.explanation: Azure CLI is a cross-platform command-line tool for managing Azure resources and can be used in shell scripts.

cards.statement: Azure PowerShell exposes Azure management operations as PowerShell cmdlets that return objects.
cards.explanation: Azure PowerShell provides cmdlets for managing Azure resources; their object output can be filtered or passed through PowerShell pipelines.

source.title: Choose the right Azure command-line tool

cards.statement: Azure Arc can manage servers running in a datacenter or another cloud as Azure resources.
cards.explanation: Azure Arc extends Azure management to servers outside Azure, including on-premises and other cloud environments.

cards.statement: Azure Resource Manager templates record a sequence of manual steps to create each resource.
cards.explanation: Azure Resource Manager templates declare the desired Azure resources and properties; Resource Manager orchestrates their deployment.
cards.misconception: ARM templates describe a step-by-step manual procedure.

cards.statement: Azure Resource Manager processes deployment requests differently in the portal and Azure CLI.
cards.explanation: Azure Resource Manager is the common management layer for requests sent through the Azure portal and Azure CLI.
cards.misconception: Portal and CLI deployments use separate management engines.

cards.statement: Azure Resource Manager deployment templates use JSON for their resource definitions and parameters.
cards.explanation: The template format is JSON; Azure Resource Manager reads its resource definitions and parameters during deployment.

cards.statement: Azure Resource Manager executes Bicep source files directly as deployment templates.
cards.explanation: During deployment, the Bicep CLI converts a Bicep file to an Azure Resource Manager JSON template.
cards.misconception: Resource Manager runs Bicep source directly rather than converting it.

cards.statement: Azure Resource Manager template deployments can target a resource group or a subscription.
cards.explanation: An ARM template deployment can target multiple Azure scopes, including a resource group and a subscription.

source.title: How to use ARM deployment templates with Azure CLI

cards.statement: Azure Advisor groups recommendations under cost, security, performance, reliability, and operational excellence.
cards.explanation: Azure Advisor analyzes deployed Azure resources and organizes its improvement recommendations into these categories.

cards.statement: Azure Advisor cost recommendations estimate savings for virtual machines planned for a future deployment.
cards.explanation: Azure Advisor cost recommendations analyze existing resources, such as underused virtual machines, and estimate potential savings.
cards.misconception: Advisor bases VM cost recommendations on undeployed plans.

cards.statement: Azure Service Health can alert subscribers to planned maintenance affecting their services.
cards.explanation: Azure Service Health provides a personalized view of Azure events and can send alerts about planned maintenance.

cards.statement: Azure status shows incidents filtered to the signed-in user's Azure subscriptions.
cards.explanation: Azure status shows a public, global view of Azure service issues; Azure Service Health provides a subscription-specific view.
cards.misconception: Azure status is a personalized subscription dashboard.

cards.statement: Azure Resource Health reports the current and past health of an individual Azure resource.
cards.explanation: Azure Resource Health tracks a resource's availability and health history, helping distinguish Azure platform issues from other causes.

cards.statement: Azure Monitor platform metrics for a virtual machine require an agent inside the guest OS.
cards.explanation: Azure Monitor collects platform metrics automatically from Azure resources. A guest OS agent is needed for guest metrics, not platform metrics.
cards.misconception: VM platform metrics require an agent in the guest OS.

source.title: Azure Monitor supported metrics and data collection

cards.statement: Azure Monitor routes resource logs to a Log Analytics workspace through diagnostic settings.
cards.explanation: A diagnostic setting sends a resource's logs to destinations such as a Log Analytics workspace, where Azure Monitor can analyze them.

source.title: Collect resource logs from an Azure resource

cards.statement: Log Analytics can run Kusto Query Language queries against Azure Monitor log data.
cards.explanation: Log Analytics uses Kusto Query Language to explore and analyze data in a Log Analytics workspace.

cards.statement: An Azure Monitor alert rule restarts a VM by default when its CPU metric crosses a threshold.
cards.explanation: An Azure Monitor alert rule evaluates the metric and fires an alert when its condition is met. An action group can trigger configured responses.
cards.misconception: A metric alert automatically restarts the affected VM.

cards.statement: Azure Monitor Application Insights requires a web app to run on Azure App Service.
cards.explanation: Azure Monitor Application Insights can monitor applications hosted on Azure, on-premises, or other clouds; Azure App Service hosting is optional.
cards.misconception: Application Insights works only for apps hosted on Azure App Service.
